# Part A - Examples of Conditional Statements

## Example A - if ... else

```{r}
score <- 78

if (score >= 75) {
  print("Passed")
} else {
  print("Failed")
}
```

## Example B - if ... else if ... else

```{r}
score <- 86

if (score >= 90) {
  print("Excellent")
} else if (score >= 80) {
  print("Good")
} else if (score >= 75) {
  print("Fair")
} else {
  print("Needs Improvement")
}
```

## Example C - ifelse()

```{r}
scores <- c(92, 68, 75, 81, 59)

ifelse(scores >= 75, "Passed", "Failed")
```

## Example D - Combining conditions

```{r}
grade <- 91
attendance <- 95

if (grade >= 90 & attendance >= 90) {
  print("Honors candidate")
}
```

# Part B - Conditional Statements

## Question #1

```{r}
temp <- 33

if (temp >= 32) {
  print("Hot")
} else {
  print("Not hot")
}
```

## Question #2

```{r}
age <- 17

if (age < 13) {
  print("Child")
} else if (age <= 19) {
  print("Teenager")
} else {
  print("Adult")
}
```

## Question #3

```{r}
marks <- c(45, 88, 73, 100, 62)

result <- ifelse(marks >= 60, "Pass", "Fail")

result
```

## Question #4

```{r}
x <- 10

if (x > 5) {
  print("A")
} else if (x > 8) {
  print("B")
} else {
  print("C")
}
```

```{r}
## The output is "A" because x is 10 and satisfies the first condition, x > 5.
## R executes the first TRUE condition and skips the remaining conditions.
```

## Question #5

```{r}
## if() checks one condition and executes a block of code if the condition is TRUE.
## ifelse() checks a vector and returns a corresponding value for each element.
## I would use if() for individual decisions and ifelse() for vectorized comparisons.
```

## Question #6(f) - Applying Conditional Statements

### f.1 Compute the final grade

```{r}
grades$FinalGrade <- 0.30 * grades$Quiz +
                     0.30 * grades$Midterm +
                     0.40 * grades$Final

grades$FinalGrade
```

```{r}
## The final grade is calculated using 30% of the Quiz, 30% of the Midterm, and 40% of the Final.
## Any missing score produces NA as the final grade, which is expected.
```

### f.2 Pass or fail

```{r}
grades$Result <- ifelse(is.na(grades$FinalGrade),
                        "Incomplete",
                        ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 75,
                               "Passed",
                               "Failed"))

grades$Result
```

```{r}
## Missing final grades are checked first because NA cannot be directly classified as Passed or Failed.
## Students with complete scores are classified based on whether their grade is at least 75.
```

### f.3 Grade remarks

```{r}
grades$Remarks <- ifelse(is.na(grades$FinalGrade), "Incomplete",
                  ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 90, "Excellent",
                  ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 85, "Very Good",
                  ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 80, "Good",
                  ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 75, "Fair",
                         "Needs Improvement")))))

grades$Remarks
```

```{r}
## Remarks are assigned according to the final grade.
## Missing grades are marked Incomplete, while the other grades use the given cutoffs.
```

### f.4 Attendance flag

```{r}
grades$AttendanceFlag <- ifelse(grades$Attendance < 80,
                               "At Risk",
                               "OK")

grades$AttendanceFlag
```

```{r}
## Students with attendance below 80 are marked At Risk.
## Students with attendance of 80 or higher are marked OK.
```

### f.5 Honors candidates

```{r}
grades$Honors <- ifelse(is.na(grades$FinalGrade),
                        "No",
                        ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 90 & grades$Attendance >= 90,
                               "Yes",
                               "No"))

grades$Honors
```

```{r}
## A student qualifies for honors only if the final grade and attendance are both at least 90.
## Students with missing final grades are automatically assigned No.
```

### f.6 if ... else if inside a loop

```{r}
remarks_loop <- rep(NA, nrow(grades))

for (i in 1:nrow(grades)) {
  if (is.na(grades$FinalGrade[i])) {
    remarks_loop[i] <- "Incomplete"
  } else if (grades$FinalGrade[i] >= 90) {
    remarks_loop[i] <- "Excellent"
  } else if (grades$FinalGrade[i] >= 85) {
    remarks_loop[i] <- "Very Good"
  } else if (grades$FinalGrade[i] >= 80) {
    remarks_loop[i] <- "Good"
  } else if (grades$FinalGrade[i] >= 75) {
    remarks_loop[i] <- "Fair"
  } else {
    remarks_loop[i] <- "Needs Improvement"
  }
}

remarks_loop
```

```{r}
## A loop allows if() and else if() to evaluate one student at a time.
## Each student's final grade is checked until the appropriate remark is assigned.
```

### f.7 Test if on its own

```{r, eval=FALSE}
if (grades$FinalGrade >= 75) {
  print("Passed")
}
```

```{r}
## This produces an error because if() expects a single TRUE or FALSE value.
## grades$FinalGrade contains multiple values and may also contain NA.
## The loop version avoids this by checking one student's grade at a time.
```




# Part D - Exporting Results to CSV

## Question #7(a) - Export the full processed table

```{r}
write.csv(grades, "students_grades_processed.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

## Question #7(b) - Export the at-risk students

```{r}
at_risk <- grades[grades$AttendanceFlag == "At Risk", ]

if (nrow(at_risk) > 0) {
  write.csv(at_risk, "at_risk_students.csv", row.names = FALSE)
  print("At-risk students exported successfully")
} else {
  print("There are no at-risk students")
}
```

## Question #7(c) - Export the honors list

### Create the honors data frame

```{r}
honors <- grades[grades$Honors == "Yes",
                  c("StudentID", "Name", "Section", "FinalGrade", "Attendance")]

honors
```

### Export the honors list

```{r}
if (nrow(honors) > 0) {
  write.csv(honors, "honors_list.csv", row.names = FALSE)
  print("Honors list exported successfully")
} else {
  print("There are no honors candidates")
}
```

# Question #9 - Scholarship

## (a) 

```{r}
grades$Scholarship <- ifelse(is.na(grades$FinalGrade),
                             "Pending",
                     ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 95 & grades$Attendance >= 90,
                            "Full",
                     ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 85 & grades$Attendance >= 90,
                            "Partial",
                            "None")))

grades$Scholarship
```

## (b) 

```{r}
## Missing grades are checked first and assigned Pending. Students with a grade of 95 or higher and attendance of at least 90 receive Full. Students with a grade of 85 or higher and attendance of at least 90 receive Partial. 

## Everyone else receives None.
```

## (c) 

```{r}
scholarship_candidates <- grades[grades$Scholarship %in% c("Full", "Partial"), ]

scholarship_candidates
```

## (d) 

```{r}
if (nrow(scholarship_candidates) > 0) {
  write.csv(scholarship_candidates,
            "scholarship_candidates.csv",
            row.names = FALSE)
  print("Scholarship candidates exported successfully")
} else {
  print("There are no scholarship candidates")
}
```

## (e) Print a count of each category

```{r}
table(grades$Scholarship)
```

# Question #10

```{r}
## 1. I checked is.na() first because missing grades cannot be properly compared with 75. Checking for NA first prevents the condition from returning an undefined result.
```

```{r}
## 2. If the Failed condition comes before Incomplete, missing grades may not be properly classified. Checking Incomplete first ensures that missing grades are handled before numerical comparisons.
```

```{r}
## 3. ifelse() is better when checking an entire vector because it evaluates each element automatically. if ... else is better when making a decision for one value or executing multiple statements.
```

```{r}
## 4. Reading an exported CSV back into R allows us to verify that the file was saved correctly.It also helps check whether the columns, values, and missing data were preserved.
```
